messages.subject: non parametric occupancy model error
parts:
Hello, 
Wondering if anyone can help me with this error:

I'm attempting to run the non-parmetric occupancy model (from the Turek 2021 paper, https://hal.science/hal-03367099/document)  

here is my code, etc:

nimble model: 

occ_long_nonpar_dot <- nimbleCode({
 
  psi ~ dunif(0,1)
 
  alpha ~ dgamma(1, 1)
  xi[1:n_sites] ~ dCRP(conc=alpha, size=n_sites)
  for(i in 1:M) p[i] ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
  for (i in 1:n_sites) {    # Loop over sites
    Z[i] ~ dbern(psi)
    for (j in 1:n_reps[i]) {  # loop over reps
     
      y[rep.index[i,j]] ~ dbern(p[xi[i]] * Z[i])
     
    }
   
  }
})



M = n.sites.in

dat<-list(y = y.in
)

const<-list(
  M = M,
  n_sites = n.sites.in,
  n_reps = start.stop.index$n.reps.by.site,
  rep.index = start.stop.index$site.rep.index
)

init<- list(
  p = rep(0.5,M),
  Z = rep(1, n.sites.in),
  alpha=1,
  xi=rep(1,n.sites.in)
)

params = c(
           'Z',
           'p',
           'psi'        
)

run.model<-nimbleModel(
  code = occ_long_nonpar_dot ,
  constants = const,
  data = dat,
  inits = init
)

.n.iter <- 10000
.n.burnin <- 500
.n.thin <- 10

model.config<-configureMCMC(run.model,
 monitors = params, 
onlySlice = F, enableWAIC = T
)


mcmc.model<-buildMCMC(model.config)

c.mcmc.model<-compileNimble(run.model, mcmc.model)

samples<-runMCMC(c.mcmc.model$mcmc.model,
                 #mcmc.model,
                 niter = .n.iter,
                 nburnin = .n.burnin,
                 thin = .n.thin,
                 summary = T,
                 WAIC = T)

At buildMCMC I am getting the following error:

Error in samplerFunction(model = model, mvSaved = mvSaved, target = target,  :
  sampler_CRP: The number of nodes that are jointly clustered must be the same for each group. For example if 'mu[i,j]' are clustered such that all nodes for a given 'i' must be in the same cluster, then the number of nodes for each 'i' must be the same. Group 1 has 27 nodes being clustered where 29.123809523809523 are expected.

My capture history is long form with uneven replicates by site (hence the j indexing in the model), I though this might be the problem so I padded the reps with NA's to make them even length (by site), but I still received the same error. this same data set does run in a simple occupancy model (with the crp code removed).  Hopefully this isn't a simple error in my model code that I am missing.  

I have attached an rds including everything needed to run and reproduce the error, in case that helps.

Thank you,
Brian

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: non parametric occupancy model error
parts:
Brian, this is a great question, and this comes down to a current (implementation) restriction of the dCRP distribution (and the associated samplers).

Basically, for each unit being clustered - in this case the units are the 210 sites - at present nimble requires that there be the same number of observation nodes within each unit.  In your case, the number of observations within each unit are specified by the n_reps[] vector, which are certainly not all the same.  Here, as the error message is trying to convey, the first clustinger unit (site = i = 1) has n_reps[1] = 27 observations in it, which is not equal to what nimble is hoping (actually, requiring) for each group, that there be length(y) / 210 = 29.12381 observations in each group.  Yes, I know it doesn't make sense with the rounding, but that's the gist of things here.

I apologize for this shortcoming in this system.  That said, you'll be able to work around this using a custom distribution, where for each value of i, you define one "observation" that follows your custom-written distribution, which accepts a vector of all the real observation values for that site (value of i), and also accepts the current cluster membership for that observation (or, more accurately, the values of p[xi[i]] and Z[i]), and calculates and returns the joint likelihood of these observations.  This will work, because now each clustering unit (site) will have exactly 1 "observation" associated with it.

Does this make sense?

Cheers,
Daniel

Hi Daniel,

Thanks for getting back to me.  Can you elaborate a little bit on your suggested work around.. a couple of questions that maybe help demonstrate my confusion.  Would I modify the code for the distribution function dCRP to accept the vector for each i ? I dug around a little bit and see that the error is in the sampler function (sample_CRP).  from your suggestion I am getting that if I modify the distribution to see each i as a single observation, rather than each rep being a single observation, I can get the sampler to accept my code.. or something like that?

I also attempted to run this code as a stick breaking problem.. I used the examples in the manual to modify my crp code:

occ_long_nonpar_stickbreak_dot <- nimbleCode({

for(i in 1:(L-1)){
    v[i] ~ dbeta(1, alpha)
  }
  w[1:L] <- stick_breaking(v[1:(L-1)])

  for(i in 1:L) p[i] ~ dunif(0, 1)

for (i in 1:n_sites) {    # Loop over sites
    Z[i] ~ dbern(psi)

y[rep.index[i,j]] ~ dbern(p[s[i]] * Z[i])
     
    }
   
  }
})


this runs with my dataset as is (in long form, uneven),  does this look correct to you for a simple occ model?  also, in your paper you make a graph of the posterior samples of subgroups.  Is there an equivalent analysis for the stick breaking model?  I see in the stick breaking model that I ran, that I get the same number of p's (detection rates) as my L input variable, which makes sense. So in an analysis of real data would I do something like decrease my L, number of breaks, over multiple model runs untill waic starts to rise (then look at model fit, residuals, autocorrelation...)?   

Sorry for the barrage of questions,  as you can tell I am climbing up the non-parametric modeling learning curve here.

Thank you for the help,
Brian

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: non parametric occupancy model error
parts:
Brian, sorry I wasn't clear.  My suggestion was to create a vectorized version of the dbern() distribution, so that for each value of i, instead of the dependencies of xi[i] being the n_reps[i] different declarations:

y[rep.index[i, j]] ~ dbern(p[xi[i]] * Z[i])         ## for all values of j = 1 ... n_reps[i]

the dependencies would rather be:

y[ 1:new_contant_vector_that_you_define[i] ] ~ dYourNewDistribution( p[xi[i]]*Z[i] )  

Yes, the stick-breaking form that you implemented will also get around this problem, and will lead to a valid model and MCMC.  The important difference will be the sampling mechanism using by nimble for each case, which will be different.  Details and links for more information about this are available in Section 10.4 of the user manual.  I myself have used the dCRP representation more extensively, and have found the collapsed sampler operating jointly on the xi[] vector works well.  But feel free to try either one.

No, you should not try restricting (lowering) the value of L.  The point of these models is that L is "large enough" to allow the data to dictate how many subgroups are populated.  To make a similar analysis of the subgroups using the stick-breaking model, you would look at the values of the s[] variable for group membership, which assumes the role of the x[] variable from the CRP model.

Cheers,
Daniel
